newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai celebrates HK return with mass choirs.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai celebrates HK return with mass choirs.

text.p: China's largest city, Shanghai, on Monday heralded the return of Hong Kong to China with a sing-along by 10,000 people on the banks of the Huangpu River in the city centre.

Against a backdrop of the city's colonial landmark buildings on the Bund, choirs from government offices and state factories ran through revolutionary classics and pop songs to mark the return of the British Colony to Chinese rule at midnight (1600 GMT).
"It's been over 150 years (since Britain took Hong Kong) and the common people are moved," said government worker He Futong.
"This a major event for the Chinese people," added a middle-aged auto worker. "I hope to go to Hong Kong in the future."

The drab green uniforms of the People's Liberation Army mingled with colourful minority costumes during the hour-long performance, with the singers arranged on temporary rostrums facing each other across the river.
The programme included songs such as "Without the Communist Party there would be no New China", and a recent pop song called "1997".

Police shut down major thoroughfares in central Shanghai for the celebrations, and officials estimated that 100,000 people thronged the central area despite overcast skies and official encouragement to stay at home to reduce congestion.
